summary: Submitted a combined obligation-and-check product for the bootstrap partial-state responsibility (action=check embedding a candidate with action=obligation, plus plan and harness). Claim C-bootstrap-partial-state (kind=obligation, concern=bounded_liveness) fixes one attributed responsibility: BootstrapCluster must not leave a store reporting existing state unless the bootstrap configuration entry was durably stored, so a store call failure must leave the server bootstrappable. Grounding cites the new S-api-bootstrap (api.go:239-284) and S-api-hasstate (api.go:462-492) plus S-stablestore, with the verified binding BND-bootstrap-order (symbol BootstrapCluster, lines 261-281) covering the ordered term write and configuration-entry store; scope is bounded to a fresh store with one failing StoreLog call, excluding healthy stores and the RecoverCluster operator path. The check calls BootstrapCluster with a single simulated StoreLog failure, observes HasExistingState, then retries on the healthy store and asserts retry_allowed (retry error nil and a positive log index); the prerequisite bootstrap_attempt (first_error true, store_log_failed true) admits the operation and identity is the storage label. Construction in a scratch copy showed the retry rejected with 'bootstrap only works on new clusters' and a log index of zero, so the partial bootstrap blocks retries; that local run is construction knowledge only and the trusted runner's clean-copy execution is requested. A feedback block carries retained source ownership for the narrowed counterevidence/unknowns. Preflight returned valid:true against map v9, and the run's four earlier confirmed_in_scope conclusions across five implementation_reproduced findings are unchanged.
